```json
{"targets": [
  {"metric": "tpd", "op": "<=", "value": 2.0e-9},
  {"metric": "power", "op": "<=", "value": 21e-6},
  {"metric": "polarity_ok", "op": ">=", "value": 1}
],
"topology": "NMOS diff-pair preamp (PMOS mirror) + push-pull PMOS-CS second stage (NMOS pull-down mirrored from preamp diode side) + CMOS inverter",
"rationale": "VCM=0.9 V with |Vtp|~1 V rules out a PMOS input pair, so the input pair is NMOS. The second stage is push-pull: when the input changes, its pull-up falls and its pull-down rises together, which removes the slow current-starved edge. All devices use short L for small node capacitance. Static current about 2 (IREF) + 4 + 1 + 4 uA, roughly 20 uW. The inverter gives rail-to-rail drive into 50 fF and draws no static current."}
```

```python
PARAMS = {
    "gmid_in": (18.0, 12.0, 22.0),
    "L_in":    (0.18, 0.15, 0.5),
    "Itail":   (4e-6, 2e-6, 6e-6),
    "I2":      (4e-6, 2e-6, 6e-6),
    "I6":      (1.0e-6, 0.5e-6, 2e-6),
    "gmid_p":  (12.0, 8.0, 15.0),
    "L_p":     (0.25, 0.15, 0.6),
    "gmid_nb": (12.0, 8.0, 16.0),
    "Wp_inv":  (3.0, 1.0, 8.0),
}

def design(p, lut, spec):
    iref = spec.get("iref", 2e-6)
    vod = spec.get("vod", 0.01)
    cl = spec.get("cl", 50e-15)
    It, I2, I6 = p["Itail"], p["I2"], p["I6"]
    Lnb = 0.5

    # bias: ibias diode + tail mirror (same gm/Id, L)
    mb = lut.size("n", p["gmid_nb"], Lnb, iref, vds=0.6)
    mt = lut.size("n", p["gmid_nb"], Lnb, It, vds=0.3)
    # input pair
    m1 = lut.size("n", p["gmid_in"], p["L_in"], It / 2, vds=0.5, vsb=0.3)
    # PMOS mirror load; M5 / M6 copy it (same gm/Id, L, scaled Id)
    m3 = lut.size("p", p["gmid_p"], p["L_p"], It / 2, vds=0.9)
    m5 = lut.size("p", p["gmid_p"], p["L_p"], I2, vds=0.9)
    m6 = lut.size("p", p["gmid_p"], p["L_p"], I6, vds=0.9)
    # NMOS mirror: M7 diode (I6) -> M8 pull-down (I2)
    m7 = lut.size("n", p["gmid_nb"], Lnb, I6, vds=0.7)
    m8 = lut.size("n", p["gmid_nb"], Lnb, I2, vds=0.9)

    n = Netlist("vinp vinn vout vdd vss ibias")
    n.dev("MB", "ibias", "ibias", "vss", "vss", mb)
    n.dev("MT", "tail", "ibias", "vss", "vss", mt)
    n.dev("M1", "d1", "vinp", "tail", "vss", m1)
    n.dev("M2", "o1", "vinn", "tail", "vss", m1)
    n.dev("M3", "d1", "d1", "vdd", "vdd", m3)
    n.dev("M4", "o1", "d1", "vdd", "vdd", m3)
    # push-pull second stage
    n.dev("M5", "o2", "o1", "vdd", "vdd", m5)      # pull-up, falls when vinp>vinn
    n.dev("M6", "d6", "d1", "vdd", "vdd", m6)      # copies vinp-side current
    n.dev("M7", "d6", "d6", "vss", "vss", m7)
    n.dev("M8", "o2", "d6", "vss", "vss", m8)      # pull-down, rises when vinp>vinn
    # output inverter (o2 low -> vout high)
    Wn, Wp = 1.0, p["Wp_inv"]
    n.M("MIN", "vout", "o2", "vss", "vss", "nfet", Wn, 0.15)
    n.M("MIP", "vout", "o2", "vdd", "vdd", "pfet", Wp, 0.15)

    # first-order delay model
    cox = 8.5e-15  # F/um^2
    c_inv = (Wn + Wp) * 0.15 * cox * 1.5
    C1 = m1.cdd + m3.cdd + m5.cgg + 1e-15
    C2 = m5.cdd + m8.cdd + c_inv + 1e-15
    gm1 = m1.gm
    ro1 = 1.0 / (m1.gds + m3.gds)
    A1 = gm1 * ro1
    tau1 = C1 * ro1
    t1 = tau1 * math.log(2.0) if A1 * vod > 0.1 else tau1 * 1.0
    # second stage: push-pull, roughly 1.5*I2 is available near the trip point
    t2 = C2 * 0.7 / (1.5 * I2)
    I_inv = 150e-6
    t3 = cl * 0.9 / I_inv
    tpd = t1 + t2 + t3

    power = 1.8 * (iref + It + I6 + I2)
    return n, {"tpd": tpd, "power": power, "polarity_ok": 1,
               "gain1_db": db(A1)}
```

The program has not been run or simulated yet, so the predicted delay and power are first-order estimates only.

- **Reference current is assumed:** the testbench constants don't give a value for IREF, so the program assumes 2 µA. If the real reference current is much larger, the 24.4 µW power limit gets tight. The total allows about 13.5 µA, and this design draws roughly 11 µA including the 2 µA.
- **Delay is the closest spec:** the target is 2.0 ns against the 2.31 ns limit. Most of the delay comes from the input stage moving its output node with only a 10 mV overdrive.
